young-climate-leaders-in-africa-financin.headline: Young Climate Leaders in Africa - Financing & Green Economy Jobs
young-climate-leaders-in-africa-financin.author: Bob Genga
young-climate-leaders-in-africa-financin.core: Posted in last 7 days Young Climate Leaders in Africa - Financing & Green Economy Jobs I have been following some of the conversations coming out of COP31, particularly those around young people and climate change. Something caught my attention. The African Union has been talking about moving beyond youth representation in climate negotiations. The United Nations has also been pushing for more meaningful youth participation in climate, peace and security decisions. These are important conversations. But I keep coming back to one question. What happens after young people leave these conferences? We have young Africans studying climate science, negotiating climate policies, building businesses around renewable energy, researching sustainable agriculture and working with communities dealing with droughts, floods and food insecurity. Some are already in rooms where decisions are being made. Others are trying to get into those rooms. And many are doing the actual work in communities that rarely feature in international climate conversations. There is an economic dimension to this that I think deserves more attention. Who is financing young people's climate innovations? What opportunities will the transition to a green economy create? Are African governments creating the right conditions for young people to participate in this emerging economy? I don't think we should discuss Africa's climate future without listening to the people who will spend the longest time living with the consequences of today's decisions. I would like to hear from the people working in this space. At The African Diary, we are opening our microphones to young climate negotiators, researchers, environmental activists, policymakers, sustainability professionals and entrepreneurs working on climate solutions across Africa. If this is your area of work, or you know someone whose perspective deserves to be heard, we would like to have a conversation. I am interested in the work you are doing, the things you are questioning and the opportunities you think Africa is missing. Let's talk.

cybersecurity-experts-podcast-on-people-.core: Posted in last 7 days Cybersecurity Experts - Podcast On People, Decisions & Trust 🔐 You lock your front door every night. But what about the digital doors to your business? Most of us never think about cybersecurity until something goes wrong. A strange email. A stolen password. A system that suddenly stops working. And then comes the question nobody wants to ask: “How did we let this happen?” 🎙️ In Episode 16 of Secure by Design, powered by SECNORA®, I had the pleasure of hosting Patrick Angel - MBA, CISSP AWSC CISM CRISC CISA SSM RSS, who has spent over 20 years helping organizations protect themselves from digital threats. What I enjoyed most about this conversation was that we didn't just talk about technology. We talked about people. Decisions. Trust. And why even smart companies make simple mistakes. A few things that stood out to me during our chat: 🔹 You don't need to be a technology expert to take cybersecurity seriously. 🔹 Buying more security tools doesn't automatically make your business safer. 🔹 Your employees can be your strongest defense, or your biggest weakness. 🔹 Good cybersecurity starts with asking the right questions, not buying the most expensive solutions. And perhaps my favorite takeaway is..... Cybersecurity is a lot like insurance. Nobody gets excited about it until the day they really need it. 😄 Patrick brought years of experience, practical advice, and a refreshingly down-to-earth perspective to our discussion. Whether you're running a startup, managing a business, or just wondering how safe your digital life really is, I think you'll enjoy this episode. 🎧 Watch our conversation here: [https://lnkd.in/dES7vKrj] Patrick, thank you for joining me! It was a pleasure having you on the show. 👍 Enjoyed the conversation? Hit the Subscribe button, follow Secure by Design, and share this episode with someone who should hear it! longterm-residents-of-czechia-navigating.author: Elizabeth Zahradnicek-Haas
longterm-residents-of-czechia-navigating.core: Posted in last 7 days Long-Term Residents of Czechia - Navigating Identity & Integration It seems that starting your own publication has become something of a rite of passage among laid-off, let-go, or otherwise unemployed editors. From what I've seen coming out of Prague's community of journalists lately, it's company I'm happy to be in. After 20 years of reporting on Czechia, I've launched Czechish.cz, an independent publication for everyone whose lives cross cultures. I wanted to create something for people who have lived here long enough to feel almost completely, but not quite, Czech. People with Czech partners, families, friends, and colleagues who still have meaningful questions about the relationships, institutions, and policies that impact our lives. Over the past two months, I've been reporting on everything from crisis preparedness and Prague's integration strategy to bilingual children navigating Czech schools and skilled professionals so invisible to a government recruiting 'foreign workers' that they end up working in fast food. I've also met some extraordinary people along the way, including a kung fu teacher whose dumplings have kept an unlikely group of friends together for 14 years and so many experts and fellow journalists who were generously gave their time to a publication that didn't even has a logo yet. Some of that reporting is now live on Czechish.cz. But this is very much a work in progress. I aim to build a publication that readers actually need and use, rather than add to the volume of content already competing for their attention. If you work in journalism, research, education, public policy, or simply have a story about life in Czechia that deserves closer attention, I'd love to hear from you. Read Czechish: https://www.czechish.cz Take our reader survey: https://lnkd.in/d2Ffh8NH Follow Czechish on Instagram: @czech_ish And on Facebook: @czechish Czechish

south-africans-with-autoimmune-disease-d.core: Posted in last 7 days South Africans With Autoimmune Disease - Diagnosis Delays HAVE YOU EVER FELT LIKE YOUR SYMPTOMS WEREN’T TAKEN SERIOUSLY? A new international study of more than 6,600 people with autoimmune diseases has found a striking gender gap in the journey to diagnosis. Women were more likely than men to report having symptoms attributed to psychiatric or psychosomatic causes, and they also reported longer waits before receiving the correct diagnosis. Autoimmune conditions such as lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and multiple sclerosis can be difficult to diagnose, particularly when early symptoms include fatigue, pain or other symptoms that aren’t always visible. We’d like to hear from South Africans living with autoimmune conditions. How long did it take you to get a diagnosis? Were you initially given another explanation for your symptoms, and did you feel listened to by your healthcare providers? #CarteBlanche #SouthAfrica #Health #AutoimmuneDisease Carte Blanche
